page: OVHcloud a10-45 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for compute-heavy workloads. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9554 processor with 30 physical cores and 30 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 42.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.4 GB per core, and includes a local 400 GB SSD. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA A10 GPU based on the Ampere architecture, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance runs on a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across both CPU and GPU tasks. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, as well as Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is mixed, with small-block cached read bandwidth placing in the top 25%, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. In database operations, the server demonstrates strong performance, highlighted by a Redis SET throughput of 72.39 million operations per second. For artificial intelligence workloads, the NVIDIA A10 GPU delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference for small and medium models. However, a notable tradeoff is observed with large models, where text generation speed drops to a poor 2.39 tokens per second, though prompt processing remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a balanced resource density for specialized workloads, combining dedicated high-core-count AMD EPYC execution with a professional-grade Ampere GPU without the premium cost of ultra-high-end accelerator tiers. This hardware profile is highly suited for medium-scale machine learning inference, data science pipelines, parallelized decompression tasks, and database operations. It is less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation due to VRAM and memory bandwidth limitations on massive models.
